<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_distribute_group_doc"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>DISTRIBUTE_GROUP_DOC</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a65_DISTRIBUTE_5FGROUP_5FDOC" name="a65_DISTRIBUTE_5FGROUP_5FDOC"></a> If member grouping is used in the documentation and the <code>DISTRIBUTE_GROUP_DOC</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then Doxygen will reuse the documentation of the first member in the group (if any) for the other members of the group. By default all members of a group must be documented explicitly.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_group_nested_compounds"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>GROUP_NESTED_COMPOUNDS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a66_GROUP_5FNESTED_5FCOMPOUNDS" name="a66_GROUP_5FNESTED_5FCOMPOUNDS"></a> If one adds a struct or class to a group and this option is enabled, then also any nested class or struct is added to the same group. By default this option is disabled and one has to add nested compounds explicitly via <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdingroup">\ingroup</a>.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_subgrouping"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>SUBGROUPING</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a67_SUBGROUPING" name="a67_SUBGROUPING"></a> Set the <code>SUBGROUPING</code> tag to <code>YES</code> to allow class member groups of the same type (for instance a group of public functions) to be put as a subgroup of that type (e.g. under the Public Functions section). Set it to <code>NO</code> to prevent subgrouping. Alternatively, this can be done per class using the <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdnosubgrouping">\nosubgrouping</a> command.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_inline_grouped_classes"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>INLINE_GROUPED_CLASSES</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a68_INLINE_5FGROUPED_5FCLASSES" name="a68_INLINE_5FGROUPED_5FCLASSES"></a> When the <code>INLINE_GROUPED_CLASSES</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code>, classes, structs and unions are shown inside the group in which they are included (e.g. using <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdingroup">\ingroup</a>) instead of on a separate page (for HTML and Man pages) or section (for <img class="formulaInl light-mode-visible" alt="$\mbox{\LaTeX}$" src="form_11.png" width="34" height="13"/><img class="formulaInl dark-mode-visible" alt="$\mbox{\LaTeX}$" src="form_11_dark.png" width="34" height="13"/> and RTF). <br  />
Note that this feature does not work in combination with <a class="el" href="#cfg_separate_member_pages">SEPARATE_MEMBER_PAGES</a>.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_inline_simple_structs"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>INLINE_SIMPLE_STRUCTS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a69_INLINE_5FSIMPLE_5FSTRUCTS" name="a69_INLINE_5FSIMPLE_5FSTRUCTS"></a> When the <code>INLINE_SIMPLE_STRUCTS</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code>, structs, classes, and unions with only public data fields or simple typedef fields will be shown inline in the documentation of the scope in which they are defined (i.e. file, namespace, or group documentation), provided this scope is documented. If set to <code>NO</code>, structs, classes, and unions are shown on a separate page (for HTML and Man pages) or section (for <img class="formulaInl light-mode-visible" alt="$\mbox{\LaTeX}$" src="form_11.png" width="34" height="13"/><img class="formulaInl dark-mode-visible" alt="$\mbox{\LaTeX}$" src="form_11_dark.png" width="34" height="13"/> and RTF).</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_typedef_hides_struct"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>TYPEDEF_HIDES_STRUCT</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a70_TYPEDEF_5FHIDES_5FSTRUCT" name="a70_TYPEDEF_5FHIDES_5FSTRUCT"></a> When <code>TYPEDEF_HIDES_STRUCT</code> tag is enabled, a typedef of a struct, union, or enum is documented as struct, union, or enum with the name of the typedef. So <code>typedef struct TypeS {} TypeT</code>, will appear in the documentation as a struct with name <code>TypeT</code>. When disabled the typedef will appear as a member of a file, namespace, or class. And the struct will be named <code>TypeS</code>. This can typically be useful for C code in case the coding convention dictates that all compound types are typedef'ed and only the typedef is referenced, never the tag name.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_lookup_cache_size"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>LOOKUP_CACHE_SIZE</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a71_LOOKUP_5FCACHE_5FSIZE" name="a71_LOOKUP_5FCACHE_5FSIZE"></a> The size of the symbol lookup cache can be set using <code>LOOKUP_CACHE_SIZE</code>. This cache is used to resolve symbols given their name and scope. Since this can be an expensive process and often the same symbol appears multiple times in the code, Doxygen keeps a cache of pre-resolved symbols. If the cache is too small Doxygen will become slower. If the cache is too large, memory is wasted. The cache size is given by this formula: <img class="formulaInl light-mode-visible" alt="$2^{(16+\mbox{LOOKUP\_CACHE\_SIZE})}$" src="form_12.png" width="166" height="15"/><img class="formulaInl dark-mode-visible" alt="$2^{(16+\mbox{LOOKUP\_CACHE\_SIZE})}$" src="form_12_dark.png" width="166" height="15"/>. The valid range is 0..9, the default is 0, corresponding to a cache size of <img class="formulaInl light-mode-visible" alt="$2^{16} = 65536$" src="form_13.png" width="65" height="11"/><img class="formulaInl dark-mode-visible" alt="$2^{16} = 65536$" src="form_13_dark.png" width="65" height="11"/> symbols. At the end of a run Doxygen will report the cache usage and suggest the optimal cache size from a speed point of view.</p>
<p class="interdd">Minimum value: <code>0</code>, maximum value: <code>9</code>, default value: <code>0</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_num_proc_threads"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>NUM_PROC_THREADS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a72_NUM_5FPROC_5FTHREADS" name="a72_NUM_5FPROC_5FTHREADS"></a> The <code>NUM_PROC_THREADS</code> specifies the number of threads Doxygen is allowed to use during processing. When set to <code>0</code> Doxygen will based this on the number of cores available in the system. You can set it explicitly to a value larger than 0 to get more control over the balance between CPU load and processing speed. At this moment only the input processing can be done using multiple threads. Since this is still an experimental feature the default is set to 1, which effectively disables parallel processing. Please report any issues you encounter. Generating dot graphs in parallel is controlled by the <code>DOT_NUM_THREADS</code> setting.</p>
<p class="interdd">Minimum value: <code>0</code>, maximum value: <code>32</code>, default value: <code>1</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_timestamp"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>TIMESTAMP</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a73_TIMESTAMP" name="a73_TIMESTAMP"></a> If the <code>TIMESTAMP</code> tag is set different from <code>NO</code> then each generated page will contain the date or date and time when the page was generated. Setting this to <code>NO</code> can help when comparing the output of multiple runs.</p>
<p class="interdd">Possible values are: <code>YES</code>, <code>NO</code>, <code>DATETIME</code> and <code>DATE</code>.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"></p>
</dd>
</dl>
<h1 class="doxsection"><a class="anchor" id="config_build"></a>
Build related configuration options</h1>
<p><a class="anchor" id="cfg_extract_all"></a></p><dl>
<dt><code>EXTRACT_ALL</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a74_EXTRACT_5FALL" name="a74_EXTRACT_5FALL"></a> If the <code>EXTRACT_ALL</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code>, Doxygen will assume all entities in documentation are documented, even if no documentation was available. Private class members and static file members will be hidden unless the <a class="el" href="#cfg_extract_private">EXTRACT_PRIVATE</a> respectively <a class="el" href="#cfg_extract_static">EXTRACT_STATIC</a> tags are set to <code>YES</code>.</p>
<dl class="section note"><dt>Note</dt><dd>This will also disable the warnings about undocumented members that are normally produced when <a class="el" href="#cfg_warnings">WARNINGS</a> is set to <code>YES</code>.</dd></dl>
<p>The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_extract_private"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>EXTRACT_PRIVATE</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a75_EXTRACT_5FPRIVATE" name="a75_EXTRACT_5FPRIVATE"></a> If the <code>EXTRACT_PRIVATE</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code>, all private members of a class will be included in the documentation.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_extract_priv_virtual"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>EXTRACT_PRIV_VIRTUAL</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a76_EXTRACT_5FPRIV_5FVIRTUAL" name="a76_EXTRACT_5FPRIV_5FVIRTUAL"></a> If the <code>EXTRACT_PRIV_VIRTUAL</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code>, documented private virtual methods of a class will be included in the documentation.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_extract_package"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>EXTRACT_PACKAGE</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a77_EXTRACT_5FPACKAGE" name="a77_EXTRACT_5FPACKAGE"></a> If the <code>EXTRACT_PACKAGE</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code>, all members with package or internal scope will be included in the documentation.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_extract_static"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>EXTRACT_STATIC</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a78_EXTRACT_5FSTATIC" name="a78_EXTRACT_5FSTATIC"></a> If the <code>EXTRACT_STATIC</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code>, all static members of a file will be included in the documentation.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_extract_local_classes"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>EXTRACT_LOCAL_CLASSES</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a79_EXTRACT_5FLOCAL_5FCLASSES" name="a79_EXTRACT_5FLOCAL_5FCLASSES"></a> If the <code>EXTRACT_LOCAL_CLASSES</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code>, classes (and structs) defined locally in source files will be included in the documentation. If set to <code>NO</code>, only classes defined in header files are included. Does not have any effect for Java sources.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_extract_local_methods"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>EXTRACT_LOCAL_METHODS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a80_EXTRACT_5FLOCAL_5FMETHODS" name="a80_EXTRACT_5FLOCAL_5FMETHODS"></a> This flag is only useful for Objective-C code. If set to <code>YES</code>, local methods, which are defined in the implementation section but not in the interface are included in the documentation. If set to <code>NO</code>, only methods in the interface are included.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_extract_anon_nspaces"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>EXTRACT_ANON_NSPACES</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a81_EXTRACT_5FANON_5FNSPACES" name="a81_EXTRACT_5FANON_5FNSPACES"></a> If this flag is set to <code>YES</code>, the members of anonymous namespaces will be extracted and appear in the documentation as a namespace called 'anonymous_namespace{file}', where file will be replaced with the base name of the file that contains the anonymous namespace. By default anonymous namespace are hidden.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_resolve_unnamed_params"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>RESOLVE_UNNAMED_PARAMS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a82_RESOLVE_5FUNNAMED_5FPARAMS" name="a82_RESOLVE_5FUNNAMED_5FPARAMS"></a> If this flag is set to <code>YES</code>, the name of an unnamed parameter in a declaration will be determined by the corresponding definition. By default unnamed parameters remain unnamed in the output.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_hide_undoc_members"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>HIDE_UNDOC_MEMBERS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a83_HIDE_5FUNDOC_5FMEMBERS" name="a83_HIDE_5FUNDOC_5FMEMBERS"></a> If the <code>HIDE_UNDOC_MEMBERS</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code>, Doxygen will hide all undocumented members inside documented classes or files. If set to <code>NO</code> these members will be included in the various overviews, but no documentation section is generated. This option has no effect if <a class="el" href="#cfg_extract_all">EXTRACT_ALL</a> is enabled.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_hide_undoc_classes"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>HIDE_UNDOC_CLASSES</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a84_HIDE_5FUNDOC_5FCLASSES" name="a84_HIDE_5FUNDOC_5FCLASSES"></a> If the <code>HIDE_UNDOC_CLASSES</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code>, Doxygen will hide all undocumented classes that are normally visible in the class hierarchy. If set to <code>NO</code>, these classes will be included in the various overviews. This option will also hide undocumented C++ concepts if enabled. This option has no effect if <a class="el" href="#cfg_extract_all">EXTRACT_ALL</a> is enabled.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_hide_undoc_namespaces"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>HIDE_UNDOC_NAMESPACES</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a85_HIDE_5FUNDOC_5FNAMESPACES" name="a85_HIDE_5FUNDOC_5FNAMESPACES"></a> If the <code>HIDE_UNDOC_NAMESPACES</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code>, Doxygen will hide all undocumented namespaces that are normally visible in the namespace hierarchy. If set to <code>NO</code>, these namespaces will be included in the various overviews. This option has no effect if <a class="el" href="#cfg_extract_all">EXTRACT_ALL</a> is enabled.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_hide_friend_compounds"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>HIDE_FRIEND_COMPOUNDS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a86_HIDE_5FFRIEND_5FCOMPOUNDS" name="a86_HIDE_5FFRIEND_5FCOMPOUNDS"></a> If the <code>HIDE_FRIEND_COMPOUNDS</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code>, Doxygen will hide all friend declarations. If set to <code>NO</code>, these declarations will be included in the documentation.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_hide_in_body_docs"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>HIDE_IN_BODY_DOCS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a87_HIDE_5FIN_5FBODY_5FDOCS" name="a87_HIDE_5FIN_5FBODY_5FDOCS"></a> If the <code>HIDE_IN_BODY_DOCS</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code>, Doxygen will hide any documentation blocks found inside the body of a function. If set to <code>NO</code>, these blocks will be appended to the function's detailed documentation block.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_internal_docs"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>INTERNAL_DOCS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a88_INTERNAL_5FDOCS" name="a88_INTERNAL_5FDOCS"></a> The <code>INTERNAL_DOCS</code> tag determines if documentation that is typed after a <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdinternal">\internal</a> command is included. If the tag is set to <code>NO</code> then the documentation will be excluded. Set it to <code>YES</code> to include the internal documentation.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_case_sense_names"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>CASE_SENSE_NAMES</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a89_CASE_5FSENSE_5FNAMES" name="a89_CASE_5FSENSE_5FNAMES"></a> With the correct setting of option <code>CASE_SENSE_NAMES</code> Doxygen will better be able to match the capabilities of the underlying filesystem.</p>
<p class="interdd">In case the filesystem is case sensitive (i.e. it supports files in the same directory whose names only differ in casing), the option must be set to <code>YES</code> to properly deal with such files in case they appear in the input.</p>
<p class="interdd">For filesystems that are not case sensitive the option should be set to <code>NO</code> to properly deal with output files written for symbols that only differ in casing, such as for two classes, one named <code>CLASS</code> and the other named <code>Class</code>, and to also support references to files without having to specify the exact matching casing.</p>
<p class="interdd">On Windows (including Cygwin) and macOS, users should typically set this option to <code>NO</code>, whereas on Linux or other Unix flavors it should typically be set to <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="interdd">Possible values are: <code>SYSTEM</code>, <code>NO</code> and <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>SYSTEM</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_hide_scope_names"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>HIDE_SCOPE_NAMES</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a90_HIDE_5FSCOPE_5FNAMES" name="a90_HIDE_5FSCOPE_5FNAMES"></a> If the <code>HIDE_SCOPE_NAMES</code> tag is set to <code>NO</code> then Doxygen will show members with their full class and namespace scopes in the documentation. If set to <code>YES</code>, the scope will be hidden.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_hide_compound_reference"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>HIDE_COMPOUND_REFERENCE</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a91_HIDE_5FCOMPOUND_5FREFERENCE" name="a91_HIDE_5FCOMPOUND_5FREFERENCE"></a> If the <code>HIDE_COMPOUND_REFERENCE</code> tag is set to <code>NO</code> (default) then Doxygen will append additional text to a page's title, such as Class Reference. If set to <code>YES</code> the compound reference will be hidden.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_show_headerfile"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>SHOW_HEADERFILE</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a92_SHOW_5FHEADERFILE" name="a92_SHOW_5FHEADERFILE"></a> If the <code>SHOW_HEADERFILE</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then the documentation for a class will show which file needs to be included to use the class.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_show_include_files"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>SHOW_INCLUDE_FILES</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a93_SHOW_5FINCLUDE_5FFILES" name="a93_SHOW_5FINCLUDE_5FFILES"></a> If the <code>SHOW_INCLUDE_FILES</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then Doxygen will put a list of the files that are included by a file in the documentation of that file.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_show_grouped_memb_inc"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>SHOW_GROUPED_MEMB_INC</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a94_SHOW_5FGROUPED_5FMEMB_5FINC" name="a94_SHOW_5FGROUPED_5FMEMB_5FINC"></a> If the <code>SHOW_GROUPED_MEMB_INC</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then Doxygen will add for each grouped member an include statement to the documentation, telling the reader which file to include in order to use the member.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_force_local_includes"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>FORCE_LOCAL_INCLUDES</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a95_FORCE_5FLOCAL_5FINCLUDES" name="a95_FORCE_5FLOCAL_5FINCLUDES"></a> If the <code>FORCE_LOCAL_INCLUDES</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then Doxygen will list include files with double quotes in the documentation rather than with sharp brackets.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_inline_info"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>INLINE_INFO</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a96_INLINE_5FINFO" name="a96_INLINE_5FINFO"></a> If the <code>INLINE_INFO</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then a tag [inline] is inserted in the documentation for inline members.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_sort_member_docs"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>SORT_MEMBER_DOCS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a97_SORT_5FMEMBER_5FDOCS" name="a97_SORT_5FMEMBER_5FDOCS"></a> If the <code>SORT_MEMBER_DOCS</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then Doxygen will sort the (detailed) documentation of file and class members alphabetically by member name. If set to <code>NO</code>, the members will appear in declaration order.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_sort_brief_docs"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>SORT_BRIEF_DOCS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a98_SORT_5FBRIEF_5FDOCS" name="a98_SORT_5FBRIEF_5FDOCS"></a> If the <code>SORT_BRIEF_DOCS</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then Doxygen will sort the brief descriptions of file, namespace and class members alphabetically by member name. If set to <code>NO</code>, the members will appear in declaration order. Note that this will also influence the order of the classes in the class list.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_sort_members_ctors_1st"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>SORT_MEMBERS_CTORS_1ST</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a99_SORT_5FMEMBERS_5FCTORS_5F1ST" name="a99_SORT_5FMEMBERS_5FCTORS_5F1ST"></a> If the <code>SORT_MEMBERS_CTORS_1ST</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then Doxygen will sort the (brief and detailed) documentation of class members so that constructors and destructors are listed first. If set to <code>NO</code> the constructors will appear in the respective orders defined by <a class="el" href="#cfg_sort_brief_docs">SORT_BRIEF_DOCS</a> and <a class="el" href="#cfg_sort_member_docs">SORT_MEMBER_DOCS</a>. </p><dl class="section note"><dt>Note</dt><dd>If <a class="el" href="#cfg_sort_brief_docs">SORT_BRIEF_DOCS</a> is set to <code>NO</code> this option is ignored for sorting brief member documentation. </dd>
<dd>
If <a class="el" href="#cfg_sort_member_docs">SORT_MEMBER_DOCS</a> is set to <code>NO</code> this option is ignored for sorting detailed member documentation.</dd></dl>
<p>The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_sort_group_names"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>SORT_GROUP_NAMES</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a100_SORT_5FGROUP_5FNAMES" name="a100_SORT_5FGROUP_5FNAMES"></a> If the <code>SORT_GROUP_NAMES</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then Doxygen will sort the hierarchy of group names into alphabetical order. If set to <code>NO</code> the group names will appear in their defined order.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_sort_by_scope_name"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>SORT_BY_SCOPE_NAME</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a101_SORT_5FBY_5FSCOPE_5FNAME" name="a101_SORT_5FBY_5FSCOPE_5FNAME"></a> If the <code>SORT_BY_SCOPE_NAME</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code>, the class list will be sorted by fully-qualified names, including namespaces. If set to <code>NO</code>, the class list will be sorted only by class name, not including the namespace part. </p><dl class="section note"><dt>Note</dt><dd>This option is not very useful if <a class="el" href="#cfg_hide_scope_names">HIDE_SCOPE_NAMES</a> is set to <code>YES</code>. </dd>
<dd>
This option applies only to the class list, not to the alphabetical list.</dd></dl>
<p>The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_strict_proto_matching"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>STRICT_PROTO_MATCHING</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a102_STRICT_5FPROTO_5FMATCHING" name="a102_STRICT_5FPROTO_5FMATCHING"></a> If the <code>STRICT_PROTO_MATCHING</code> option is enabled and Doxygen fails to do proper type resolution of all parameters of a function it will reject a match between the prototype and the implementation of a member function even if there is only one candidate or it is obvious which candidate to choose by doing a simple string match. By disabling <code>STRICT_PROTO_MATCHING</code> Doxygen will still accept a match between prototype and implementation in such cases.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_generate_todolist"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>GENERATE_TODOLIST</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a103_GENERATE_5FTODOLIST" name="a103_GENERATE_5FTODOLIST"></a> The <code>GENERATE_TODOLIST</code> tag can be used to enable (<code>YES</code>) or disable (<code>NO</code>) the todo list. This list is created by putting <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdtodo">\todo</a> commands in the documentation.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_generate_testlist"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>GENERATE_TESTLIST</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a104_GENERATE_5FTESTLIST" name="a104_GENERATE_5FTESTLIST"></a> The <code>GENERATE_TESTLIST</code> tag can be used to enable (<code>YES</code>) or disable (<code>NO</code>) the test list. This list is created by putting <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdtest">\test</a> commands in the documentation.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_generate_buglist"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>GENERATE_BUGLIST</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a105_GENERATE_5FBUGLIST" name="a105_GENERATE_5FBUGLIST"></a> The <code>GENERATE_BUGLIST</code> tag can be used to enable (<code>YES</code>) or disable (<code>NO</code>) the bug list. This list is created by putting <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdbug">\bug</a> commands in the documentation.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_generate_deprecatedlist"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>GENERATE_DEPRECATEDLIST</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a106_GENERATE_5FDEPRECATEDLIST" name="a106_GENERATE_5FDEPRECATEDLIST"></a> The <code>GENERATE_DEPRECATEDLIST</code> tag can be used to enable (<code>YES</code>) or disable (<code>NO</code>) the deprecated list. This list is created by putting <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmddeprecated">\deprecated</a> commands in the documentation.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_enabled_sections"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>ENABLED_SECTIONS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a107_ENABLED_5FSECTIONS" name="a107_ENABLED_5FSECTIONS"></a> The <code>ENABLED_SECTIONS</code> tag can be used to enable conditional documentation sections, marked by <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdif">\if</a> <section_label> ... <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdendif">\endif</a> and <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdcond">\cond</a> <section_label> ... <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdendcond">\endcond</a> blocks.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_max_initializer_lines"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>MAX_INITIALIZER_LINES</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a108_MAX_5FINITIALIZER_5FLINES" name="a108_MAX_5FINITIALIZER_5FLINES"></a> The <code>MAX_INITIALIZER_LINES</code> tag determines the maximum number of lines that the initial value of a variable or macro / define can have for it to appear in the documentation. If the initializer consists of more lines than specified here it will be hidden. Use a value of 0 to hide initializers completely. The appearance of the value of individual variables and macros / defines can be controlled using <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdshowinitializer">\showinitializer</a> or <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdhideinitializer">\hideinitializer</a> command in the documentation regardless of this setting.</p>
<p class="interdd">Minimum value: <code>0</code>, maximum value: <code>10000</code>, default value: <code>30</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_show_used_files"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>SHOW_USED_FILES</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a109_SHOW_5FUSED_5FFILES" name="a109_SHOW_5FUSED_5FFILES"></a> Set the <code>SHOW_USED_FILES</code> tag to <code>NO</code> to disable the list of files generated at the bottom of the documentation of classes and structs. If set to <code>YES</code>, the list will mention the files that were used to generate the documentation.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_show_files"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>SHOW_FILES</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a110_SHOW_5FFILES" name="a110_SHOW_5FFILES"></a> Set the <code>SHOW_FILES</code> tag to <code>NO</code> to disable the generation of the Files page. This will remove the Files entry from the Quick Index and from the Folder Tree View (if specified).</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_show_namespaces"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>SHOW_NAMESPACES</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a111_SHOW_5FNAMESPACES" name="a111_SHOW_5FNAMESPACES"></a> Set the <code>SHOW_NAMESPACES</code> tag to <code>NO</code> to disable the generation of the Namespaces page. This will remove the Namespaces entry from the Quick Index and from the Folder Tree View (if specified).</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_file_version_filter"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>FILE_VERSION_FILTER</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a112_FILE_5FVERSION_5FFILTER" name="a112_FILE_5FVERSION_5FFILTER"></a> The <code>FILE_VERSION_FILTER</code> tag can be used to specify a program or script that Doxygen should invoke to get the current version for each file (typically from the version control system). Doxygen will invoke the program by executing (via <code>popen()</code>) the command <code>command input-file</code>, where <code>command</code> is the value of the <code>FILE_VERSION_FILTER</code> tag, and <code>input-file</code> is the name of an input file provided by Doxygen. Whatever the program writes to standard output is used as the file version.<br  />
 <br  />
 Example of using a shell script as a filter for Unix: </p><pre class="fragment"> FILE_VERSION_FILTER = "/bin/sh versionfilter.sh"
</pre><p> <br  />
 Example shell script for CVS: </p><pre class="fragment">#!/bin/sh
cvs status $1 | sed -n 's/^[ \]*Working revision:[ \t]*\‍([0-9][0-9\.]*\‍).*/\1/p'
</pre><p> <br  />
 Example shell script for Subversion: </p><pre class="fragment">#!/bin/sh
svn stat -v $1 | sed -n 's/^[ A-Z?\*|!]\{1,15\}/r/;s/ \{1,15\}/\/r/;s/ .*//p'
</pre><p> <br  />
 Example filter for ClearCase: </p><pre class="fragment">FILE_VERSION_FILTER = "cleartool desc -fmt \%Vn"
</pre><p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_layout_file"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>LAYOUT_FILE</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a113_LAYOUT_5FFILE" name="a113_LAYOUT_5FFILE"></a> The <code>LAYOUT_FILE</code> tag can be used to specify a layout file which will be parsed by Doxygen. The layout file controls the global structure of the generated output files in an output format independent way. To create the layout file that represents Doxygen's defaults, run Doxygen with the <span class="tt">-l</span> option. You can optionally specify a file name after the option, if omitted <code>DoxygenLayout.xml</code> will be used as the name of the layout file. See also section <a class="el" href="customize.html#layout">Changing the layout of pages</a> for information. <br  />
Note that if you run Doxygen from a directory containing a file called <code>DoxygenLayout.xml</code>, Doxygen will parse it automatically even if the <code>LAYOUT_FILE</code> tag is left empty.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_cite_bib_files"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>CITE_BIB_FILES</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a114_CITE_5FBIB_5FFILES" name="a114_CITE_5FBIB_5FFILES"></a> The <code>CITE_BIB_FILES</code> tag can be used to specify one or more <code>bib</code> files containing the reference definitions. This must be a list of <code>.bib</code> files. The <code>.bib</code> extension is automatically appended if omitted. This requires the <code>bibtex</code> tool to be installed. See also <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BibTeX">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BibTeX</a> for more info. For <img class="formulaInl light-mode-visible" alt="$\mbox{\LaTeX}$" src="form_11.png" width="34" height="13"/><img class="formulaInl dark-mode-visible" alt="$\mbox{\LaTeX}$" src="form_11_dark.png" width="34" height="13"/> the style of the bibliography can be controlled using <a class="el" href="#cfg_latex_bib_style">LATEX_BIB_STYLE</a>. To use this feature you need <code>bibtex</code> and <code>perl</code> available in the search path. See also <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdcite">\cite</a> for info how to create references.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_external_tool_path"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>EXTERNAL_TOOL_PATH</code> </dt>
<dd><a id="a115_EXTERNAL_5FTOOL_5FPATH" name="a115_EXTERNAL_5FTOOL_5FPATH"></a> The <code>EXTERNAL_TOOL_PATH</code> tag can be used to extend the search path (PATH environment variable) so that external tools such as <code>latex</code> and <code>gs</code> can be found. <dl class="section note"><dt>Note</dt><dd>Directories specified with EXTERNAL_TOOL_PATH are added in front of the path already specified by the PATH variable, and are added in the order specified. </dd>
<dd>
This option is particularly useful for macOS version 14 (Sonoma) and higher, when running Doxygen from Doxywizard, because in this case any user-defined changes to the PATH are ignored. A typical example on macOS is to set <pre class="fragment">EXTERNAL_TOOL_PATH = /Library/TeX/texbin /usr/local/bin
</pre> together with the standard path, the full search path used by doxygen when launching external tools will then become <pre class="fragment">PATH=/Library/TeX/texbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin
</pre></dd></dl>
</dd>
</dl>
<h1 class="doxsection"><a class="anchor" id="config_messages"></a>
Configuration options related to warning and progress messages</h1>
<p><a class="anchor" id="cfg_quiet"></a></p><dl>
<dt><code>QUIET</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a116_QUIET" name="a116_QUIET"></a> The <code>QUIET</code> tag can be used to turn on/off the messages that are generated to standard output by Doxygen. If <code>QUIET</code> is set to <code>YES</code> this implies that the messages are off.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_warnings"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>WARNINGS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a117_WARNINGS" name="a117_WARNINGS"></a> The <code>WARNINGS</code> tag can be used to turn on/off the warning messages that are generated to standard error (<code>stderr</code>) by Doxygen. If <code>WARNINGS</code> is set to <code>YES</code> this implies that the warnings are on. <br  />
 <b>Tip:</b> Turn warnings on while writing the documentation.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_warn_if_undocumented"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>WARN_IF_UNDOCUMENTED</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a118_WARN_5FIF_5FUNDOCUMENTED" name="a118_WARN_5FIF_5FUNDOCUMENTED"></a> If the <code>WARN_IF_UNDOCUMENTED</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then Doxygen will generate warnings for undocumented members. If <a class="el" href="#cfg_extract_all">EXTRACT_ALL</a> is set to <code>YES</code> then this flag will automatically be disabled.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_warn_if_doc_error"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>WARN_IF_DOC_ERROR</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a119_WARN_5FIF_5FDOC_5FERROR" name="a119_WARN_5FIF_5FDOC_5FERROR"></a> If the <code>WARN_IF_DOC_ERROR</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code>, Doxygen will generate warnings for potential errors in the documentation, such as documenting some parameters in a documented function twice, or documenting parameters that don't exist or using markup commands wrongly.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_warn_if_incomplete_doc"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>WARN_IF_INCOMPLETE_DOC</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a120_WARN_5FIF_5FINCOMPLETE_5FDOC" name="a120_WARN_5FIF_5FINCOMPLETE_5FDOC"></a> If <code>WARN_IF_INCOMPLETE_DOC</code> is set to <code>YES</code>, Doxygen will warn about incomplete function parameter documentation. If set to <code>NO</code>, Doxygen will accept that some parameters have no documentation without warning.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_warn_no_paramdoc"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>WARN_NO_PARAMDOC</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a121_WARN_5FNO_5FPARAMDOC" name="a121_WARN_5FNO_5FPARAMDOC"></a> This <code>WARN_NO_PARAMDOC</code> option can be enabled to get warnings for functions that are documented, but have no documentation for their parameters or return value. If set to <code>NO</code>, Doxygen will only warn about wrong parameter documentation, but not about the absence of documentation. If <a class="el" href="#cfg_extract_all">EXTRACT_ALL</a> is set to <code>YES</code> then this flag will automatically be disabled. See also <a class="el" href="#cfg_warn_if_incomplete_doc">WARN_IF_INCOMPLETE_DOC</a></p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_warn_if_undoc_enum_val"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>WARN_IF_UNDOC_ENUM_VAL</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a122_WARN_5FIF_5FUNDOC_5FENUM_5FVAL" name="a122_WARN_5FIF_5FUNDOC_5FENUM_5FVAL"></a> If <code>WARN_IF_UNDOC_ENUM_VAL</code> option is set to <code>YES</code>, Doxygen will warn about undocumented enumeration values. If set to <code>NO</code>, Doxygen will accept undocumented enumeration values. If <a class="el" href="#cfg_extract_all">EXTRACT_ALL</a> is set to <code>YES</code> then this flag will automatically be disabled.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_warn_layout_file"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>WARN_LAYOUT_FILE</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a123_WARN_5FLAYOUT_5FFILE" name="a123_WARN_5FLAYOUT_5FFILE"></a> If <code>WARN_LAYOUT_FILE</code> option is set to <code>YES</code>, Doxygen will warn about issues found while parsing the user defined layout file, such as missing or wrong elements. See also <a class="el" href="#cfg_layout_file">LAYOUT_FILE</a> for details. If set to <code>NO</code>, problems with the layout file will be suppressed.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_warn_as_error"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>WARN_AS_ERROR</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a124_WARN_5FAS_5FERROR" name="a124_WARN_5FAS_5FERROR"></a> If the <code>WARN_AS_ERROR</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then Doxygen will immediately stop when a warning is encountered. If the <code>WARN_AS_ERROR</code> tag is set to <code>FAIL_ON_WARNINGS</code> then Doxygen will continue running as if <code>WARN_AS_ERROR</code> tag is set to <code>NO</code>, but at the end of the Doxygen process Doxygen will return with a non-zero status. If the <code>WARN_AS_ERROR</code> tag is set to <code>FAIL_ON_WARNINGS_PRINT</code> then Doxygen behaves like <code>FAIL_ON_WARNINGS</code> but in case no <a class="el" href="#cfg_warn_logfile">WARN_LOGFILE</a> is defined Doxygen will not write the warning messages in between other messages but write them at the end of a run, in case a <a class="el" href="#cfg_warn_logfile">WARN_LOGFILE</a> is defined the warning messages will be besides being in the defined file also be shown at the end of a run, unless the <a class="el" href="#cfg_warn_logfile">WARN_LOGFILE</a> is defined as <span class="tt">-</span> i.e. standard output (<span class="tt">stdout</span>) in that case the behavior will remain as with the setting <code>FAIL_ON_WARNINGS</code>.</p>
<p class="interdd">Possible values are: <code>NO</code>, <code>YES</code>, <code>FAIL_ON_WARNINGS</code> and <code>FAIL_ON_WARNINGS_PRINT</code>.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_warn_format"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>WARN_FORMAT</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a125_WARN_5FFORMAT" name="a125_WARN_5FFORMAT"></a> The <code>WARN_FORMAT</code> tag determines the format of the warning messages that Doxygen can produce. The string should contain the <code>$file</code>, <code>$line</code>, and <code>$text</code> tags, which will be replaced by the file and line number from which the warning originated and the warning text. Optionally the format may contain <code>$version</code>, which will be replaced by the version of the file (if it could be obtained via <a class="el" href="#cfg_file_version_filter">FILE_VERSION_FILTER</a>)</p>
<dl class="section see"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a class="el" href="#cfg_warn_line_format">WARN_LINE_FORMAT</a></dd></dl>
<p>The default value is: <code>$file:$line: $text</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_warn_line_format"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>WARN_LINE_FORMAT</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a126_WARN_5FLINE_5FFORMAT" name="a126_WARN_5FLINE_5FFORMAT"></a> In the <span class="tt">$text</span> part of the <a class="el" href="#cfg_warn_format">WARN_FORMAT</a> command it is possible that a reference to a more specific place is given. To make it easier to jump to this place (outside of Doxygen) the user can define a custom "cut" / "paste" string.</p>
<p class="interdd">Example: </p><pre class="fragment">  WARN_LINE_FORMAT = "'vi $file +$line'"
</pre><dl class="section see"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a class="el" href="#cfg_warn_format">WARN_FORMAT</a></dd></dl>
<p>The default value is: <code>at line $line of file $file</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_warn_logfile"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>WARN_LOGFILE</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a127_WARN_5FLOGFILE" name="a127_WARN_5FLOGFILE"></a> The <code>WARN_LOGFILE</code> tag can be used to specify a file to which warning and error messages should be written. If left blank the output is written to standard error (<span class="tt">stderr</span>). In case the file specified cannot be opened for writing the warning and error messages are written to standard error. When as file <span class="tt">-</span> is specified the warning and error messages are written to standard output (<span class="tt">stdout</span>).</p>
<p class="enddd"></p>
</dd>
</dl>
<h1 class="doxsection"><a class="anchor" id="config_input"></a>
Configuration options related to the input files</h1>
<p><a class="anchor" id="cfg_input"></a></p><dl>
<dt><code>INPUT</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a128_INPUT" name="a128_INPUT"></a> The <code>INPUT</code> tag is used to specify the files and/or directories that contain documented source files. You may enter file names like <code>myfile.cpp</code> or directories like <code>/usr/src/myproject</code>. Separate the files or directories with spaces. See also <a class="el" href="#cfg_file_patterns">FILE_PATTERNS</a> and <a class="el" href="#cfg_extension_mapping">EXTENSION_MAPPING</a></p>
<dl class="section note"><dt>Note</dt><dd>If this tag is empty the current directory is searched.</dd></dl>
<p><a class="anchor" id="cfg_input_encoding"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>INPUT_ENCODING</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a129_INPUT_5FENCODING" name="a129_INPUT_5FENCODING"></a> This tag can be used to specify the character encoding of the source files that Doxygen parses. Internally Doxygen uses the UTF-8 encoding. Doxygen uses <span class="tt">libiconv</span> (or the <span class="tt">iconv</span> built into <span class="tt">libc</span>) for the transcoding. See <a href="https://www.gnu.org/software/libiconv/">the libiconv documentation</a> for the list of possible encodings.</p>
<dl class="section see"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a class="el" href="#cfg_input_file_encoding">INPUT_FILE_ENCODING</a></dd></dl>
<p>The default value is: <code>UTF-8</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_input_file_encoding"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>INPUT_FILE_ENCODING</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a130_INPUT_5FFILE_5FENCODING" name="a130_INPUT_5FFILE_5FENCODING"></a> This tag can be used to specify the character encoding of the source files that Doxygen parses. The <code>INPUT_FILE_ENCODING</code> tag can be used to specify character encoding on a per file pattern basis. Doxygen will compare the file name with each pattern and apply the encoding instead of the default <a class="el" href="#cfg_input_encoding">INPUT_ENCODING</a> if there is a match. The character encodings are a list of the form: pattern=encoding (like <span class="tt">*.php=ISO-8859-1</span>).</p>
<dl class="section see"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a class="el" href="#cfg_input_encoding">INPUT_ENCODING</a> for further information on supported encodings.</dd></dl>
<p><a class="anchor" id="cfg_file_patterns"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>FILE_PATTERNS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a131_FILE_5FPATTERNS" name="a131_FILE_5FPATTERNS"></a> If the value of the <a class="el" href="#cfg_input">INPUT</a> tag contains directories, you can use the <code>FILE_PATTERNS</code> tag to specify one or more wildcard patterns (like <span class="tt">*.cpp</span> and <span class="tt">*.h</span>) to filter out the source-files in the directories.<br  />
 Note that for custom extensions or not directly supported extensions you also need to set <a class="el" href="#cfg_extension_mapping">EXTENSION_MAPPING</a> for the extension otherwise the files are not read by Doxygen.<br  />
 Note the list of default checked file patterns might differ from the list of <a class="el" href="starting.html#default_file_extension_mapping">default file extension mappings</a>.<br  />
 If left blank the following patterns are tested: <code>*.c</code>, <code>*.cc</code>, <code>*.cxx</code>, <code>*.cxxm</code>, <code>*.cpp</code>, <code>*.cppm</code>, <code>*.ccm</code>, <code>*.c++</code>, <code>*.c++m</code>, <code>*.java</code>, <code>*.ii</code>, <code>*.ixx</code>, <code>*.ipp</code>, <code>*.i++</code>, <code>*.inl</code>, <code>*.idl</code>, <code>*.ddl</code>, <code>*.odl</code>, <code>*.h</code>, <code>*.hh</code>, <code>*.hxx</code>, <code>*.hpp</code>, <code>*.h++</code>, <code>*.l</code>, <code>*.cs</code>, <code>*.d</code>, <code>*.php</code>, <code>*.php4</code>, <code>*.php5</code>, <code>*.phtml</code>, <code>*.inc</code>, <code>*.m</code>, <code>*.markdown</code>, <code>*.md</code>, <code>*.mm</code>, <code>*.dox</code> (to be provided as Doxygen C comment), <code>*.py</code>, <code>*.pyw</code>, <code>*.f90</code>, <code>*.f95</code>, <code>*.f03</code>, <code>*.f08</code>, <code>*.f18</code>, <code>*.f</code>, <code>*.for</code>, <code>*.vhd</code>, <code>*.vhdl</code>, <code>*.ucf</code>, <code>*.qsf</code> and <code>*.ice</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_recursive"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>RECURSIVE</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a132_RECURSIVE" name="a132_RECURSIVE"></a> The <code>RECURSIVE</code> tag can be used to specify whether or not subdirectories should be searched for input files as well.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_exclude"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>EXCLUDE</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a133_EXCLUDE" name="a133_EXCLUDE"></a> The <code>EXCLUDE</code> tag can be used to specify files and/or directories that should be excluded from the <a class="el" href="#cfg_input">INPUT</a> source files. This way you can easily exclude a subdirectory from a directory tree whose root is specified with the <a class="el" href="#cfg_input">INPUT</a> tag. <br  />
Note that relative paths are relative to the directory from which Doxygen is run.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_exclude_symlinks"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>EXCLUDE_SYMLINKS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a134_EXCLUDE_5FSYMLINKS" name="a134_EXCLUDE_5FSYMLINKS"></a> The <code>EXCLUDE_SYMLINKS</code> tag can be used to select whether or not files or directories that are symbolic links (a Unix file system feature) are excluded from the input.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_exclude_patterns"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>EXCLUDE_PATTERNS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a135_EXCLUDE_5FPATTERNS" name="a135_EXCLUDE_5FPATTERNS"></a> If the value of the <a class="el" href="#cfg_input">INPUT</a> tag contains directories, you can use the <code>EXCLUDE_PATTERNS</code> tag to specify one or more wildcard patterns to exclude certain files from those directories. <br  />
Note that the wildcards are matched against the file with absolute path, so to exclude all test directories for example use the pattern <span class="tt">*</span><span class="tt">/test/</span><span class="tt">*</span></p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_exclude_symbols"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>EXCLUDE_SYMBOLS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a136_EXCLUDE_5FSYMBOLS" name="a136_EXCLUDE_5FSYMBOLS"></a> The <code>EXCLUDE_SYMBOLS</code> tag can be used to specify one or more symbol names (namespaces, classes, functions, etc.) that should be excluded from the output. The symbol name can be a fully qualified name, a word, or if the wildcard <span class="tt">*</span> is used, a substring. Examples: <span class="tt">ANamespace</span>, <span class="tt">AClass</span>, <span class="tt">ANamespace::AClass</span>, <span class="tt">ANamespace::*Test</span></p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_example_path"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>EXAMPLE_PATH</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a137_EXAMPLE_5FPATH" name="a137_EXAMPLE_5FPATH"></a> The <code>EXAMPLE_PATH</code> tag can be used to specify one or more files or directories that contain example code fragments that are included (see the <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdinclude">\include</a> command).</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_example_patterns"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>EXAMPLE_PATTERNS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a138_EXAMPLE_5FPATTERNS" name="a138_EXAMPLE_5FPATTERNS"></a> If the value of the <a class="el" href="#cfg_example_path">EXAMPLE_PATH</a> tag contains directories, you can use the <code>EXAMPLE_PATTERNS</code> tag to specify one or more wildcard pattern (like <span class="tt">*.cpp</span> and <span class="tt">*.h</span>) to filter out the source-files in the directories. If left blank all files are included.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_example_recursive"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>EXAMPLE_RECURSIVE</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a139_EXAMPLE_5FRECURSIVE" name="a139_EXAMPLE_5FRECURSIVE"></a> If the <code>EXAMPLE_RECURSIVE</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then subdirectories will be searched for input files to be used with the <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdinclude">\include</a> or <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmddontinclude">\dontinclude</a> commands irrespective of the value of the <a class="el" href="#cfg_recursive">RECURSIVE</a> tag.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_image_path"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>IMAGE_PATH</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a140_IMAGE_5FPATH" name="a140_IMAGE_5FPATH"></a> The <code>IMAGE_PATH</code> tag can be used to specify one or more files or directories that contain images that are to be included in the documentation (see the <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdimage">\image</a> command).</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_input_filter"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>INPUT_FILTER</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a141_INPUT_5FFILTER" name="a141_INPUT_5FFILTER"></a> The <code>INPUT_FILTER</code> tag can be used to specify a program that Doxygen should invoke to filter for each input file. Doxygen will invoke the filter program by executing (via <code>popen()</code>) the command: <br  />
 <code><filter> <input-file></code> <br  />
 where <code><filter></code> is the value of the <code>INPUT_FILTER</code> tag, and <code><input-file></code> is the name of an input file. Doxygen will then use the output that the filter program writes to standard output. If <a class="el" href="#cfg_filter_patterns">FILTER_PATTERNS</a> is specified, this tag will be ignored. <br  />
Note that the filter must not add or remove lines; it is applied before the code is scanned, but not when the output code is generated. If lines are added or removed, the anchors will not be placed correctly. <br  />
Note that Doxygen will use the data processed and written to standard output for further processing, therefore nothing else, like debug statements or used commands (so in case of a Windows batch file always use <span class="tt">@echo OFF</span>), should be written to standard output. <br  />
Note that for custom extensions or not directly supported extensions you also need to set <a class="el" href="#cfg_extension_mapping">EXTENSION_MAPPING</a> for the extension otherwise the files are not properly processed by Doxygen.<br  />
</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_filter_patterns"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>FILTER_PATTERNS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a142_FILTER_5FPATTERNS" name="a142_FILTER_5FPATTERNS"></a> The <code>FILTER_PATTERNS</code> tag can be used to specify filters on a per file pattern basis. Doxygen will compare the file name with each pattern and apply the filter if there is a match. The filters are a list of the form: pattern=filter (like <span class="tt">*.cpp=my_cpp_filter</span>). See <a class="el" href="#cfg_input_filter">INPUT_FILTER</a> for further information on how filters are used. If the <code>FILTER_PATTERNS</code> tag is empty or if none of the patterns match the file name, <a class="el" href="#cfg_input_filter">INPUT_FILTER</a> is applied. <br  />
Note that for custom extensions or not directly supported extensions you also need to set <a class="el" href="#cfg_extension_mapping">EXTENSION_MAPPING</a> for the extension otherwise the files are not properly processed by Doxygen.<br  />
</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_filter_source_files"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>FILTER_SOURCE_FILES</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a143_FILTER_5FSOURCE_5FFILES" name="a143_FILTER_5FSOURCE_5FFILES"></a> If the <code>FILTER_SOURCE_FILES</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code>, the input filter (if set using <a class="el" href="#cfg_input_filter">INPUT_FILTER</a>) will also be used to filter the input files that are used for producing the source files to browse (i.e. when <a class="el" href="#cfg_source_browser">SOURCE_BROWSER</a> is set to <code>YES</code>).</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_filter_source_patterns"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>FILTER_SOURCE_PATTERNS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a144_FILTER_5FSOURCE_5FPATTERNS" name="a144_FILTER_5FSOURCE_5FPATTERNS"></a> The <code>FILTER_SOURCE_PATTERNS</code> tag can be used to specify source filters per file pattern. A pattern will override the setting for <a class="el" href="#cfg_filter_patterns">FILTER_PATTERN</a> (if any) and it is also possible to disable source filtering for a specific pattern using <span class="tt">*.ext=</span> (so without naming a filter).</p>
<p class="enddd">This tag requires that the tag <a class="el" href="#cfg_filter_source_files">FILTER_SOURCE_FILES</a> is set to <code>YES</code>. <a class="anchor" id="cfg_use_mdfile_as_mainpage"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>USE_MDFILE_AS_MAINPAGE</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a145_USE_5FMDFILE_5FAS_5FMAINPAGE" name="a145_USE_5FMDFILE_5FAS_5FMAINPAGE"></a> If the <code>USE_MDFILE_AS_MAINPAGE</code> tag refers to the name of a markdown file that is part of the input, its contents will be placed on the main page (<span class="tt">index.html</span>). This can be useful if you have a project on for instance GitHub and want to reuse the introduction page also for the Doxygen output.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_implicit_dir_docs"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>IMPLICIT_DIR_DOCS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a146_IMPLICIT_5FDIR_5FDOCS" name="a146_IMPLICIT_5FDIR_5FDOCS"></a> If the <code>IMPLICIT_DIR_DOCS</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code>, any <span class="tt">README.md</span> file found in sub-directories of the project's root, is used as the documentation for that sub-directory, except when the <span class="tt">README.md</span> starts with a <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmddir">\dir</a>, <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdpage">\page</a> or <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdmainpage">\mainpage</a> command. If set to <code>NO</code>, the <span class="tt">README.md</span> file needs to start with an explicit <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmddir">\dir</a> command in order to be used as directory documentation.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_fortran_comment_after"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>FORTRAN_COMMENT_AFTER</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a147_FORTRAN_5FCOMMENT_5FAFTER" name="a147_FORTRAN_5FCOMMENT_5FAFTER"></a> The Fortran standard specifies that for fixed formatted Fortran code all characters from position 72 are to be considered as comment. A common extension is to allow longer lines before the automatic comment starts. The setting <code>FORTRAN_COMMENT_AFTER</code> will also make it possible that longer lines can be processed before the automatic comment starts.</p>
<p class="interdd">Minimum value: <code>7</code>, maximum value: <code>10000</code>, default value: <code>72</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"></p>
</dd>
</dl>
<h1 class="doxsection"><a class="anchor" id="config_source_browser"></a>
Configuration options related to source browsing</h1>
<p><a class="anchor" id="cfg_source_browser"></a></p><dl>
<dt><code>SOURCE_BROWSER</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a148_SOURCE_5FBROWSER" name="a148_SOURCE_5FBROWSER"></a> If the <code>SOURCE_BROWSER</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then a list of source files will be generated. Documented entities will be cross-referenced with these sources. <br  />
Note: To get rid of all source code in the generated output, make sure that also <a class="el" href="#cfg_verbatim_headers">VERBATIM_HEADERS</a> is set to <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_inline_sources"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>INLINE_SOURCES</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a149_INLINE_5FSOURCES" name="a149_INLINE_5FSOURCES"></a> Setting the <code>INLINE_SOURCES</code> tag to <code>YES</code> will include the body of functions, multi-line macros, enums or list initialized variables directly into the documentation.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_strip_code_comments"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>STRIP_CODE_COMMENTS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a150_STRIP_5FCODE_5FCOMMENTS" name="a150_STRIP_5FCODE_5FCOMMENTS"></a> Setting the <code>STRIP_CODE_COMMENTS</code> tag to <code>YES</code> will instruct Doxygen to hide any special comment blocks from generated source code fragments. Normal C, C++ and Fortran comments will always remain visible.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_referenced_by_relation"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>REFERENCED_BY_RELATION</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a151_REFERENCED_5FBY_5FRELATION" name="a151_REFERENCED_5FBY_5FRELATION"></a> If the <code>REFERENCED_BY_RELATION</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then for each documented entity all documented functions referencing it will be listed.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_references_relation"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>REFERENCES_RELATION</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a152_REFERENCES_5FRELATION" name="a152_REFERENCES_5FRELATION"></a> If the <code>REFERENCES_RELATION</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then for each documented function all documented entities called/used by that function will be listed.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_references_link_source"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>REFERENCES_LINK_SOURCE</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a153_REFERENCES_5FLINK_5FSOURCE" name="a153_REFERENCES_5FLINK_5FSOURCE"></a> If the <code>REFERENCES_LINK_SOURCE</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> and <a class="el" href="#cfg_source_browser">SOURCE_BROWSER</a> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then the hyperlinks from functions in <a class="el" href="#cfg_references_relation">REFERENCES_RELATION</a> and <a class="el" href="#cfg_referenced_by_relation">REFERENCED_BY_RELATION</a> lists will link to the source code. Otherwise they will link to the documentation.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_source_tooltips"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>SOURCE_TOOLTIPS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a154_SOURCE_5FTOOLTIPS" name="a154_SOURCE_5FTOOLTIPS"></a> If <code>SOURCE_TOOLTIPS</code> is enabled (the default) then hovering a hyperlink in the source code will show a tooltip with additional information such as prototype, brief description and links to the definition and documentation. Since this will make the HTML file larger and loading of large files a bit slower, you can opt to disable this feature.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd">This tag requires that the tag <a class="el" href="#cfg_source_browser">SOURCE_BROWSER</a> is set to <code>YES</code>. <a class="anchor" id="cfg_use_htags"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>USE_HTAGS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a155_USE_5FHTAGS" name="a155_USE_5FHTAGS"></a> If the <code>USE_HTAGS</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then the references to source code will point to the HTML generated by the <code>htags(1)</code> tool instead of Doxygen built-in source browser. The <code>htags</code> tool is part of GNU's global source tagging system (see <a href="https://www.gnu.org/software/global/global.html">https://www.gnu.org/software/global/global.html</a>). You will need version 4.8.6 or higher. <br  />
 To use it do the following:</p><ol type="1">
<li>Install the latest version of <code>global</code> </li>
<li>Enable <a class="el" href="#cfg_source_browser">SOURCE_BROWSER</a> and <code>USE_HTAGS</code> in the configuration file</li>
<li>Make sure the <a class="el" href="#cfg_input">INPUT</a> points to the root of the source tree</li>
<li>Run <code>doxygen</code> as normal <br  />
 Doxygen will invoke <code>htags</code> (and that will in turn invoke <code>gtags</code>), so these tools must be available from the command line (i.e. in the search path). <br  />
 The result: instead of the source browser generated by Doxygen, the links to source code will now point to the output of <code>htags</code>.</li>
</ol>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd">This tag requires that the tag <a class="el" href="#cfg_source_browser">SOURCE_BROWSER</a> is set to <code>YES</code>. <a class="anchor" id="cfg_verbatim_headers"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>VERBATIM_HEADERS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a156_VERBATIM_5FHEADERS" name="a156_VERBATIM_5FHEADERS"></a> If the <code>VERBATIM_HEADERS</code> tag is set the <code>YES</code> then Doxygen will generate a verbatim copy of the header file for each class for which an include is specified. Set to <code>NO</code> to disable this. </p><dl class="section see"><dt>See also</dt><dd>Section <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdclass">\class</a>.</dd></dl>
<p>The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_clang_assisted_parsing"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>CLANG_ASSISTED_PARSING</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a157_CLANG_5FASSISTED_5FPARSING" name="a157_CLANG_5FASSISTED_5FPARSING"></a> If the <code>CLANG_ASSISTED_PARSING</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then Doxygen will use the <a href="http://clang.llvm.org/">clang parser</a> for more accurate parsing at the cost of reduced performance. This can be particularly helpful with template rich C++ code for which Doxygen's built-in parser lacks the necessary type information.</p>
<dl class="section note"><dt>Note</dt><dd>The availability of this option depends on whether or not Doxygen was generated with the <span class="tt">-Duse_libclang=ON</span> option for CMake.</dd></dl>
<p>The default value is: <code>NO</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_clang_add_inc_paths"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>CLANG_ADD_INC_PATHS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a158_CLANG_5FADD_5FINC_5FPATHS" name="a158_CLANG_5FADD_5FINC_5FPATHS"></a> If the <code>CLANG_ASSISTED_PARSING</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> and the <code>CLANG_ADD_INC_PATHS</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code> then Doxygen will add the directory of each input to the include path.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd">This tag requires that the tag <a class="el" href="#cfg_clang_assisted_parsing">CLANG_ASSISTED_PARSING</a> is set to <code>YES</code>. <a class="anchor" id="cfg_clang_options"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>CLANG_OPTIONS</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a159_CLANG_5FOPTIONS" name="a159_CLANG_5FOPTIONS"></a> If clang assisted parsing is enabled you can provide the compiler with command line options that you would normally use when invoking the compiler. Note that the include paths will already be set by Doxygen for the files and directories specified with <a class="el" href="#cfg_input">INPUT</a> and <a class="el" href="#cfg_include_path">INCLUDE_PATH</a>.</p>
<p class="enddd">This tag requires that the tag <a class="el" href="#cfg_clang_assisted_parsing">CLANG_ASSISTED_PARSING</a> is set to <code>YES</code>. <a class="anchor" id="cfg_clang_database_path"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>CLANG_DATABASE_PATH</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a160_CLANG_5FDATABASE_5FPATH" name="a160_CLANG_5FDATABASE_5FPATH"></a> If clang assisted parsing is enabled you can provide the clang parser with the path to the directory containing a file called <span class="tt">compile_commands.json</span>. This file is the <a href="http://clang.llvm.org/docs/HowToSetupToolingForLLVM.html">compilation database</a> containing the options used when the source files were built. This is equivalent to specifying the <span class="tt">-p</span> option to a clang tool, such as <span class="tt">clang-check</span>. These options will then be passed to the parser. Any options specified with <a class="el" href="#cfg_clang_options">CLANG_OPTIONS</a> will be added as well.</p>
<dl class="section note"><dt>Note</dt><dd>The availability of this option depends on whether or not Doxygen was generated with the <span class="tt">-Duse_libclang=ON</span> option for CMake.</dd></dl>
</dd>
</dl>
<h1 class="doxsection"><a class="anchor" id="config_index"></a>
Configuration options related to the alphabetical class index</h1>
<p><a class="anchor" id="cfg_alphabetical_index"></a></p><dl>
<dt><code>ALPHABETICAL_INDEX</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a161_ALPHABETICAL_5FINDEX" name="a161_ALPHABETICAL_5FINDEX"></a> If the <code>ALPHABETICAL_INDEX</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code>, an alphabetical index of all compounds will be generated. Enable this if the project contains a lot of classes, structs, unions or interfaces.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_ignore_prefix"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>IGNORE_PREFIX</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a162_IGNORE_5FPREFIX" name="a162_IGNORE_5FPREFIX"></a> The <code>IGNORE_PREFIX</code> tag can be used to specify a prefix (or a list of prefixes) that should be ignored while generating the index headers. The <code>IGNORE_PREFIX</code> tag works for classes, function and member names. The entity will be placed in the alphabetical list under the first letter of the entity name that remains after removing the prefix.</p>
<p class="enddd">This tag requires that the tag <a class="el" href="#cfg_alphabetical_index">ALPHABETICAL_INDEX</a> is set to <code>YES</code>. </p>
</dd>
</dl>
<h1 class="doxsection"><a class="anchor" id="config_html"></a>
Configuration options related to the HTML output</h1>
<p><a class="anchor" id="cfg_generate_html"></a></p><dl>
<dt><code>GENERATE_HTML</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a163_GENERATE_5FHTML" name="a163_GENERATE_5FHTML"></a> If the <code>GENERATE_HTML</code> tag is set to <code>YES</code>, Doxygen will generate HTML output</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>YES</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd"><a class="anchor" id="cfg_html_output"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>HTML_OUTPUT</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a164_HTML_5FOUTPUT" name="a164_HTML_5FOUTPUT"></a> The <code>HTML_OUTPUT</code> tag is used to specify where the HTML docs will be put. If a relative path is entered the value of <a class="el" href="#cfg_output_directory">OUTPUT_DIRECTORY</a> will be put in front of it.</p>
<p class="interdd">The default directory is: <code>html</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd">This tag requires that the tag <a class="el" href="#cfg_generate_html">GENERATE_HTML</a> is set to <code>YES</code>. <a class="anchor" id="cfg_html_file_extension"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>HTML_FILE_EXTENSION</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a165_HTML_5FFILE_5FEXTENSION" name="a165_HTML_5FFILE_5FEXTENSION"></a> The <code>HTML_FILE_EXTENSION</code> tag can be used to specify the file extension for each generated HTML page (for example: <code>.htm, .php, .asp</code>).</p>
<p class="interdd">The default value is: <code>.html</code>.</p>
<p class="enddd">This tag requires that the tag <a class="el" href="#cfg_generate_html">GENERATE_HTML</a> is set to <code>YES</code>. <a class="anchor" id="cfg_html_header"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>HTML_HEADER</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a166_HTML_5FHEADER" name="a166_HTML_5FHEADER"></a> The <code>HTML_HEADER</code> tag can be used to specify a user-defined HTML header file for each generated HTML page. If the tag is left blank Doxygen will generate a standard header. <br  />
 To get valid HTML the header file that includes any scripts and style sheets that Doxygen needs, which is dependent on the configuration options used (e.g. the setting <a class="el" href="#cfg_generate_treeview">GENERATE_TREEVIEW</a>). It is highly recommended to start with a default header using </p><pre class="fragment">doxygen -w html new_header.html new_footer.html new_stylesheet.css YourConfigFile
</pre><p> and then modify the file <code>new_header.html</code>.</p>
<p class="interdd">See also section <a class="el" href="doxygen_usage.html">Doxygen usage</a> for information on how to generate the default header that Doxygen normally uses.</p>
<dl class="section note"><dt>Note</dt><dd>The header is subject to change so you typically have to regenerate the default header when upgrading to a newer version of Doxygen. The following markers have a special meaning inside the header and footer: <dl>
<dt><code>$title</code></dt>
<dd>will be replaced with the title of the page. </dd>
<dt><code>$datetime</code></dt>
<dd>will be replaced with the current date and time. </dd>
<dt><code>$date</code></dt>
<dd>will be replaced with the current date. </dd>
<dt><code>$time</code></dt>
<dd>will be replaced with the current time. </dd>
<dt><code>$year</code></dt>
<dd>will be replaces with the current year. </dd>
<dt><code>$showdate(<format>)</code></dt>
<dd>will be replaced with the current date and time according to the format as specified by <span class="tt"><format></span>. The <span class="tt"><format></span> follows the rules as specified for the <a class="el" href="commands.html#cmdshowdate">\showdate</a> command with the exception that no <span class="tt">)</span> is allowed in the <span class="tt"><format></span>. </dd>
<dt><code>$doxygenversion</code></dt>
<dd>will be replaced with the version of Doxygen </dd>
<dt><code>$projectname</code></dt>
<dd>will be replaced with the name of the project (see <a class="el" href="#cfg_project_name">PROJECT_NAME</a>) </dd>
<dt><code>$projectnumber</code></dt>
<dd>will be replaced with the project number (see <a class="el" href="#cfg_project_number">PROJECT_NUMBER</a>) </dd>
<dt><code>$projectbrief</code></dt>
<dd>will be replaced with the project brief description (see <a class="el" href="#cfg_project_brief">PROJECT_BRIEF</a>) </dd>
<dt><code>$projectlogo</code></dt>
<dd>will be replaced with the project logo (see <a class="el" href="#cfg_project_logo">PROJECT_LOGO</a>) </dd>
<dt><code>$generatedby</code></dt>
<dd>will be replaced with the output language dependent version of the text "Generated by" or when the <a class="el" href="#cfg_timestamp">TIMESTAMP</a> is set by the output language dependent version of the text "Generated on <span class="tt">$datetime</span> for <span class="tt">$projectname</span> by". </dd>
<dt><code>$stylesheet</code></dt>
<dd>will be replaced with the setting of <a class="el" href="#cfg_html_stylesheet">HTML_STYLESHEET</a> unless it is empty or the file in which case it is replaced by the default setting <span class="tt">doxygen.css</span>. </dd>
<dt><code>$extrastylesheet</code></dt>
<dd>will be replaced with the setting of <a class="el" href="#cfg_html_extra_stylesheet">HTML_EXTRA_STYLESHEET</a> including the required HTML tags for each extra stylesheet. </dd>
<dt><code>$treeview</code></dt>
<dd>will be replaced with links to the JavaScript and style sheets needed for the navigation tree (or an empty string when <a class="el" href="#cfg_generate_treeview">GENERATE_TREEVIEW</a> is disabled). </dd>
<dt><code>$search</code></dt>
<dd>will be replaced with a links to the JavaScript and style sheets needed for the search engine (or an empty string when <a class="el" href="#cfg_searchengine">SEARCHENGINE</a> is disabled). </dd>
<dt><code>$searchbox</code></dt>
<dd>will be replaced with the HTML code needed for the search box to be shown (or an empty string when <a class="el" href="#cfg_searchengine">SEARCHENGINE</a> is disabled). </dd>
<dt><code>$mathjax</code></dt>
<dd>will be replaced with a links to the JavaScript and style sheets needed for the MathJax feature (or an empty string when <a class="el" href="#cfg_use_mathjax">USE_MATHJAX</a> is disabled). </dd>
<dt><code>$relpath^</code></dt>
<dd>If <a class="el" href="#cfg_create_subdirs">CREATE_SUBDIRS</a> is enabled, the command <code>$relpath^</code> can be used to produce a relative path to the root of the HTML output directory, e.g. use <code>$relpath^doxygen.css</code>, to refer to the standard style sheet. </dd>
<dt><code>$navpath</code></dt>
<dd>will be replaced with a path as required by <a class="el" href="#cfg_generate_treeview">GENERATE_TREEVIEW</a> </dd>
</dl>
</dd></dl>
<p>To cope with differences in the layout of the header and footer that depend on configuration settings, the header can also contain special blocks that will be copied to the output or skipped depending on the configuration. Such blocks have the following form: </p><pre class="fragment"> <!--BEGIN BLOCKNAME-->
 Some context copied when condition BLOCKNAME holds
 <!--END BLOCKNAME-->
 <!--BEGIN !BLOCKNAME-->
 Some context copied when condition BLOCKNAME does not hold
 <!--END !BLOCKNAME-->
</pre><p> The following block names are supported: </p><dl>
<dt><code>DISABLE_INDEX</code></dt>
<dd>Content within this block is copied to the output if the <a class="el" href="#cfg_disable_index">DISABLE_INDEX</a> option is enabled (so when the index is disabled). </dd>
<dt><code>GENERATE_TREEVIEW</code></dt>
<dd>Content within this block is copied to the output if the <a class="el" href="#cfg_generate_treeview">GENERATE_TREEVIEW</a> option is enabled. </dd>
<dt><code>SEARCHENGINE</code></dt>
<dd>Content within this block is copied to the output if the <a class="el" href="#cfg_searchengine">SEARCHENGINE</a> option is enabled. </dd>
<dt><code>PROJECT_NAME</code></dt>
<dd>Content within the block is copied to the output if the <a class="el" href="#cfg_project_name">PROJECT_NAME</a> option is not empty. </dd>
<dt><code>PROJECT_NUMBER</code></dt>
<dd>Content within the block is copied to the output if the <a class="el" href="#cfg_project_number">PROJECT_NUMBER</a> option is not empty. </dd>
<dt><code>PROJECT_BRIEF</code></dt>
<dd>Content within the block is copied to the output if the <a class="el" href="#cfg_project_brief">PROJECT_BRIEF</a> option is not empty. </dd>
<dt><code>PROJECT_LOGO</code></dt>
<dd>Content within the block is copied to the output if the <a class="el" href="#cfg_project_logo">PROJECT_LOGO</a> option is not empty. </dd>
<dt><code>FULL_SIDEBAR</code></dt>
<dd>Content within the block is copied to the output if the <a class="el" href="#cfg_full_sidebar">FULL_SIDEBAR</a>, <a class="el" href="#cfg_disable_index">DISABLE_INDEX</a> and <a class="el" href="#cfg_generate_treeview">GENERATE_TREEVIEW</a> options are all enabled. </dd>
<dt><code>TITLEAREA</code></dt>
<dd>Content within this block is copied to the output if a title is visible at the top of each page. This is the case if either <a class="el" href="#cfg_project_name">PROJECT_NAME</a>, <a class="el" href="#cfg_project_brief">PROJECT_BRIEF</a>, <a class="el" href="#cfg_project_logo">PROJECT_LOGO</a> is filled in or if both <a class="el" href="#cfg_disable_index">DISABLE_INDEX</a> and <a class="el" href="#cfg_searchengine">SEARCHENGINE</a> are enabled. </dd>
</dl>
<p class="enddd">This tag requires that the tag <a class="el" href="#cfg_generate_html">GENERATE_HTML</a> is set to <code>YES</code>. <a class="anchor" id="cfg_html_footer"></a></p>
</dd>
<dt><code>HTML_FOOTER</code> </dt>
<dd><p class="startdd"><a id="a167_HTML_5FFOOTER" name="a167_HTML_5FFOOTER"></a> The <code>HTML_FOOTER</code> tag can be used to specify a user-defined HTML footer for each generated HTML page. If the tag is left blank Doxygen will generate a standard footer.</p>
